title: The backlog check runs at its CPU limit on CI, so a busy runner fails a pull request whose tests all pass

source.ref: #5044 on 2026-11-16: the full sweep burned 440.0 s of CPU against a 437.8 s budget with every probe passing.

detail: MEASURED 2026-11-16 on the 4-core cloud box, full sweep (--probes=all), main at 771c0ef80: 2,424 costed probes, 291 to 313 s of guard CPU across five runs, so run-to-run noise alone is about 7% while CI had 0.5% of headroom. WHERE THE TIME GOES: an empty node start costs 25 ms and 1,801 probes cost under 40 ms each (47 s together). 240 probes cost over 300 ms each and burn 201 s of 291 s (69%): 47 are over 1 s (89 s) and 193 are 300 ms to 1 s (112 s). They are the probes that start a test runner or a heavy script (SCAN-502 10.5 s, LIVE-2273 4.5 s, BLD-203 3.9 s, BLD-202 3.5 s, BLD-205 3.4 s; BLD-203 runs npx vitest on one file). This is cost spread across many probes, which the per-probe ceiling (6.5 s) is not built to see; the count-scaled total is the only assertion that does. Unexplained: this box reads about 300 s where CI read 440 s for the same sweep, so the CI figure needs its own per-probe dump before anything is retimed. RULED OUT: lane count. 2, 4 and 8 probes in flight cost 316, 303 and 297 to 313 s, so oversubscription is not what inflates the reading. SHIPPED WITH THIS ROW: one V8 compile cache shared by every probe in a sweep (NODE_COMPILE_CACHE, a temp directory removed on exit), which measured 276 to 292 s over six runs (mean 281 against 302 without), about 7% less. That is headroom, not the fix. WHAT CLOSES IT, either or both: (1) convert the 47 probes over 1 s to measure their consequence in-process instead of spawning a suite (the LIVE-034 pattern), which needs the owner's phrase per probe because it rewrites probes; (2) make the budget immune to runner speed by timing a fixed reference workload in the same run and asserting the ratio, which rewrites a test pin and also needs the owner's phrase. Do not raise BASE_CPU_MS or PER_PROBE_ALLOWANCE_MS without a paired CI and local reading (ADR-1107). UPDATE 2026-11-16 (owner picked A: make the budget relative to runner speed). The guard now prints runner-speed (one fixed piece of work per 100 probes, same lanes). Paired reading: CI checks job 73.2 ms, local box 82.6 to 87.3 ms. The same full sweep read 265.2 s on #5064's test job and 440.0 s on #5044's, a 1.66x spread on an unchanged list, so the spread is the runner. The contract test now multiplies the count-scaled total by runner-speed over a 75 ms reference, never below 1 and capped at 2.5, and fails if the runner-speed line goes missing. The per-probe ceiling (6.5 s) is NOT scaled and SCAN-502 read 10 to 20 s on the loaded local box against 3.7 s on CI: that ceiling is the next thing a slow runner trips, and it needs its own reading before it is touched. Still open: the 47 probes over 1 s. CARRIED OVER FROM HYG-243 (parked as a duplicate of this row): on #5044 the guard total was 32.7 s above what the probes reported (440.0 s against 407.3 s), far more than the 2 s base assumes; on #5064 the gap was 28.6 s (265.2 against 236.6). Nobody has attributed that CPU yet. It is work the per-probe report does not see, most likely shells and non-node children of probes. Attribute it before converting probes.

verify.evidence: Fails today: #5044's checks run printed guardCpuMs 440.0 s against a 437.8 s budget. Passes when ten checks runs in a row on main print a guard-cost line at or under 85% of the budget the contract test computes for that probe count.
